newsitem.title: THAILAND: Suu Kyi says repression worse, denies U.S. money.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi says repression worse, denies U.S. money.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi said on Thursday repression has grown in the past two years and denied receiving money from Americans as alleged by the military government.
"I'd have to say that repression has increased in the past two years," Suu Kyi told Reuters in a telephone interview on the second anniversary of her release from six years of house arrest.

In her first comments since being accused of collaborating with the United States, Suu Kyi also flatly denied a Burmese government accusation last month that she had received $85,200 in financial assistance from Americans this year to aid in subversive activities.

"I have certainly not received whatever they claimed, $85,200 I think they said, from any American source," Suu Kyi said just as the telephone line was cut off. It was impossible to reconnect with her residence again.

Suu Kyi said it was clear that the by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' (ASEAN) policy of "constructive engagement" with Burma's military rulers was not working. ASEAN was expected to admit Burma as a full member this month despite vocal opposition from Suu Kyi and many Western governments.

Suu Kyi was held under house arrest for six years. Her National League for Democracy party has been in a political standoff with the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council since her release in 1995. The SLORC refused to recognise the NLD's landslide election victory in 1990.
